previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and ongoing alcohol use, was admitted after a syncopal episode with a fall and head injury. He reported dizziness and a sensation of his implantable cardiac defibrillator firing, though device interrogation showed no recent activity. Initial evaluation revealed hypotension and lab findings consistent with dehydration, which improved with IV fluids. CT scans of the head and cervical spine showed no acute abnormalities, and a chest X-ray revealed a small right basilar opacity likely due to atelectasis. His symptoms were attributed to dehydration exacerbated by chronic alcohol use, Lasix therapy, and inappropriate use of nitroglycerin for device-pocket pain. His Lasix dose was adjusted to alternate between 20 mg and 40 mg daily, and he was counseled on hydration, avoiding alcohol, and not using nitroglycerin for non-cardiac pain. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up recommendations for primary care, liver monitoring, and device clinic evaluation for possible pocket revision.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with h/o dilated systolic CHF (EF 35%), PE, EtOH abuse, 
AFib presenting with nausea, chest pain and tachycardia. 
.
# TACHYCARDIA: unclear etiology, looks like atach vs. atrial 
flutter with 2:1 block on EKG. Pt has known h/o AFib. Most 
likely secondary to volume depletion in setting of poor PO 
intake. Also may be ___ EtOH withdrawal; EtOH positive on serum 
tox but states last drink was two days ago and has h/o 
withdrawal. Could also be opioid withdrawal. Has been ruled out 
for PE via CTA. 
**ICU Course**
Initially beta blocked, but no response, went into flutter, was 
treated with IV verapamil x2 with good transient response.  He 
was seen by cardiology who recommended PO verapamil and agreed 
to cardioversion.  The patient was successfully cardioverted to 
sinus rhythm on ___. And remained in regular rate for 24 hours 
after conversion.
.
# CHEST PAIN, EKG CHANGES: Pt c/o right-sided chest pain and 
nausea, appears diaphoretic. CEs negative x2. EKG shows lateral 
TWI, deeper than prior EKGs. Last stress test with no ischemic 
changes. Likely demand ischemia in setting of tachycardia, but 
should complete ___. Also of note, has chronic chest pain over 
site of ICD pocket. 
**ICU Course***
Complete ___ with ___ set CEs, seen by cardiology, changes were 
likely demand, improvement but residual twi laterally seen on 
previous, resumed previous cardiac meds including aspirin.
.
# EtOH ABUSE: Pt endorses h/o EtOH withdrawal. Last drink was 
___ night (one day ago). He is mildly tremulous and 
diaphoretic, could be withdrawing although positive serum EtOH 
and would be fairly early to start withdrawing. 
**ICU Course***
Patient was placed on a CIWA scale with IV ativan, he required 
minimal benzos and was found to be tolerating his care with 
agitation or aggression, his blood pressures were stable and his 
tachycardia resolved with calclium channel blockers and 
cardioversion.
.
# CHRONIC SYSTOLIC CHF: EF 35%, has ICD. Unclear etiology, pt 
reports h/o MI but no documentation in any records (cardiology 
has looked extensively). 
**The patient was continued on his home medications, his heart 
failure was likely a precipitate to his afib, which was 
resolved.  He was never fluid overloaded.  He did not require 
aggressive diuresis.
# ELEVATED LFTs: Likely secondary to EtOH abuse and vomiting. 
Has good liver synthetic function. 
**ICU Care**
The patient was kept on an ativan CIWA scale as he did have 
elevated liver enzymes c/w drinking.  These were trended and 
were decreasing throughout the stay.  CT abdomen was 
unremarkable from a liver perspective.
.
# H/O PE: no PE on CTA
**ICU Course**
Patient was not compliant with his lovenox therapy, he was 
cardioverted as he would likely not be compliant with coumadin 
and this would provide the dual benefit of rate control and 
alleviating the need for him to take daily anticoagulation. 
.
#Nausea/Vomiting
**ICU Course**
Patient with a history of gastric ulcers, had nonbloody, 
nonbilious emesis which intermittently resolved with 
anti-emetics.  He was ready for discharge then his epigastric 
pain and vomiting resumed, he was treated and called out to the 
floor for additional symptomatic management until he could 
tolerate PO.
.

need further anti-emetics, if it persists, possibly GI 
involvement

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ male with right lower lobe pulmonary embolism
diagnosed ___, on Lovenox, atrial fibrillation with systolic heart failure
post-AICD placement, had acute onset chest pain and vomiting x4 hours.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest from ___ and CT abdomen/pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Helical MDCT images were acquired through the chest before and
after the uneventful administration of 130 cc of intravenous Omnipaque.  5-,
2.5-, and 1.25-mm axial, 5-mm coronal and sagittal, and 3-mm bilateral oblique
multiplanar reformats were generated.  Abdominal CT was subsequently ordered,
and the patient was brought back for injection of additional 70 cc of
intravenous Omnipaque.  Helical MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen
and pelvis, and 5-mm axial, coronal, and sagittal multiplanar reformats were
generated.

FINDINGS:

CHEST:  There is no acute main, branch, lobar, or segmental pulmonary embolus.
Prior acute subsegmental embolus in the right lower lobe has resolved. 
Concomitant evolution of the associated pulmonary infarct, now with a
wedge-shaped area of subpleural scarring and dystrophic calcification.  Right
pleural effusion has cleared.  Chronic eccentric thrombus in the posterior
basal segment of the left lower lobe (3:48), stable over multiple
examinations.  

No pulmonary masses or focal consoldiation.  Mild retained secretions in the
trachea.  Note is made of a tracheal diverticulum at the carina.  Central
airways are patent to subsegmental levels.

Right ventricular pacemaker/AICD lead courses in expected position.  Mild
cardiomegaly persists, with trace physiologic pericardial fluid.

Note is made of mediastinal lipomatosis.  Axillary, hilar, and mediastinal
lymph nodes are not pathologically enlarged.

ABDOMEN:  There is diffuse fatty infiltration of the liver, with stable 6-mm
hypodensity in segment VII.  Gallbladder is partially collapsed.  The pancreas
is normal.  No intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilation.  The spleen is
normal in size.

The adrenals are normal.  Kidneys enhance and excrete contrast promptly and
symmetrically, without masses or hydronephrosis.

The stomach and small bowel are normal.

PELVIS:  The colon and rectum are normal.  Bladder is distended with urine,
with bilateral ureteral jets visualized.  Prostate and seminal vesicles are
prominent.  There is no free intraperitoneal fluid or air.

Multiple small retroperitoneal and mesenteric lymph nodes are present.

Chronic mild anterior compression deformity of T12, with 20% loss of anterior
height.Unchanged grade 1 retrolisthesis of L5-S1, with endplate sclerosis and
intervertebral vacuum disc phenomenon.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  No acute PE.  Resolved right lower lobe PE with evolving infarct.  Chronic
left lower lobe PE.

2.  Mild cardiomegaly.

3.  Fatty liver.
